title: Ambiguous Brand Names in Social Listening: A Query Fix Guide
summary: Ambiguous brand name social listening floods results with junk. Fix the query one change at a time and check precision on a fixed labeled sample as you go.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** To fix an ambiguous brand name social listening query, write the narrowest query that still finds your brand (an exact phrase plus a context term), add exclusion terms one at a time, and label a fixed sample of results before and after each change. That shows whether the share of relevant results rose without losing relevant posts. The pages we read document the building blocks but none presents this order, so the sequence is our suggested approach.


A brand named after an ordinary word collects posts about everything except the brand.


With an ambiguous brand name in social listening, a keyword match cannot tell your product from a festival, a song or a camping light. The junk fills dashboards and alerts, and every fix you try can also delete posts you wanted. For the opposite problem, posts a query never collects, see our[missed mentions](https://syncly.app/blog/why-social-listening-misses-brand-mentions) post.


Below: a fix order, what five vendors' pages say about exclusions, a precision log and an invented example. Everything is as of the pages we read in November 2026, and no query was run in any product.


## Why does an ambiguous brand name social listening query collect irrelevant mentions?


An ambiguous brand name social listening query collects irrelevant mentions because a keyword match reads text, not meaning: any post that contains your name qualifies, whatever it is about.


**Ambiguous brand name** : a brand name that is also a common word, a person's name, a place, an acronym or a handle used by someone else, so a keyword match returns posts about other things.


**Irrelevant mention** : a result that matches the query text but is not about the brand or product you meant.


**Context term** : a word that must appear in or near a post for a match to count, such as a product type.


**Exclusion term** : a word or phrase that removes any post containing it; Brand24's page says the more you add, the more limited the results. (Source:[Brand24, Nov 5, 2025](https://help.brand24.com/en/articles/3786682-how-to-use-required-or-excluded-keywords) )


Irrelevant results also feed alert overload, which our[alert fatigue guide](https://syncly.app/blog/social-listening-alert-fatigue-how-many-alerts-is-too-many) covers. If query collection is new to you, start with our[social listening basics](https://syncly.app/blog/how-to-use-social-listening) .


## How do you fix an ambiguous brand name social listening query, and in what order?


Change one thing at a time, from the broadest cut to the narrowest, and label a sample after each change. This is our suggested approach: the vendor pages document the building blocks, but none presents a fix order.


1.


**Split by name type.** Use one query each for the company name, the product name and handles or hashtags, so each can be checked alone. (Awario's` UNION` joins groups with their own sources and exclusions.)


2.


**Use an exact phrase for multi-word names.** (Quotes in Awario and YouScan; "Exact Match" in Sprout.)


3.


**Add a context or proximity term** for the category. Expect to lose relevant posts that never use it, and log them. (Required words in Brand24, placed next to the main keyword to require adjacency;` ~n` in Sprout;` NEAR` in Emplifi;` /N` in YouScan.)


4.


**Add exclusions one at a time, narrowest first** , a phrase before a single word. Scan the removed posts after each.


5.


**Add hashtag, handle and spelling variants** of your real brand, and exclude variants of the noise term.


6.


**Filter by source, language or location** where the noise sits in one place, and check what a location filter drops.


7.


**Re-sample and log.** Repeat from step 3 only if the log says so; mute or blacklist persistent junk sources last. (Brand24 mutes authors or domains; Awario has a Blacklist.)


## What do vendor help pages say about excluding irrelevant mentions?


Five vendors' pages document exclusions, and they split in two: typed in the query in Awario and YouScan, entered in a separate field or condition in Brand24, Sprout and Emplifi. Brand24 also names Boolean` NOT` , and Awario also has a separate Blacklist. "Not published" means not published on the pages we opened; "undated" means the page shows no calendar date. Emplifi is per its Listening General Guide; the docs also list a newer Listening Hub guide we did not open.

Awario's sample-queries page groups keywords in brackets so that` AND NOT` applies to every term in the group (Source:[Awario, undated, checked Nov 2026](https://awario.com/help/boolean-search/sample-queries-and-common-mistakes/) ). Its irrelevant-results page says results containing any of the excluded keywords next to your main keywords are not collected. For a furniture brand whose name is shared with a pizza restaurant, it suggests negative keywords first, then blacklisting accounts that still promote other companies, and lists three steps: the most specific request, a blacklist after the first results, then a revised search (Source:[Awario, undated, checked Nov 2026](https://awario.com/help/troubleshooting/irrelevant-results/) ).


Brand24's page advises excluding variants too, such as the hashtag form. Sprout also offers an Exclude Noise option that uses common noise categories; we did not open the category list (Source:[Sprout Social, undated, checked Nov 2026](https://support.sproutsocial.com/hc/en-us/articles/360017807291-Social-Listening-Query-Builder) ).


## How do you check precision before and after each change?


Label a fixed sample before and after each change, then count relevant results and surviving relevant posts.


**Precision** : the share of returned results that are relevant, meaning true positives divided by everything classified as positive.


**Recall** : the share of all relevant posts that the query returned, meaning true positives divided by all actual positives.


Both definitions come from a machine-learning page whose examples are spam classifiers; it says the two often show an inverse relationship. Mapping them onto listening results is our suggested approach, adapted from a machine-learning definition. (Source:[Google for Developers, Jan 12, 2026](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification/accuracy-precision-recall) )


Our suggested sample-and-log method:


1.


Write one sentence defining "relevant" and keep it fixed.


2.


Pull a fixed-size sample, one you can label in one sitting, and label each result relevant or not.


3.


Log results returned and relevant, then change one thing.


4.


Draw a fresh sample, label it and log it. Replaying the change on the old sample is only a pre-check; tools may behave differently.


5.


Scan the removed results and log relevant posts lost. The sample cannot show relevant posts the query never returned.


**Hypothetical example.** "Lantern" is an invented lip balm; no real brand is meant, and every number is illustrative and not to be generalized. The query strings are generic and untested. ## Where do tools behave differently, and what can go wrong?


Tools differ in where an exclusion goes, whether edits reach past data and whether a preview exists.


-


**Over-exclusion.** Brand24's page says more excluded words limit results; the example above shows an exclusion can cost relevant posts.


-


**Edits to past versus future data.** Brand24 applies exclusions only to mentions collected after you add them, and Emplifi applies edits to future mentions unless you duplicate the query over a past range. Sprout says existing topic data is reprocessed to remove messages that no longer match. For how tools define their window, see our[historical data by tool](https://syncly.app/blog/social-listening-historical-data-what-12-tools-mean-(2026)) post.


-


**Preview.** Only Sprout's page mentions a preview; none of the other vendor pages we opened does.


-


**Handles versus names.** Sprout's page says its from-user and mention terms work best with X, and Emplifi's page lets a keyword be plain text, a hashtag or an @mention.


-


**Misspellings and variants.** Sprout's page says keywords match as entered, so add variants yourself.


-


**Query length.** Emplifi's page says length counts filters and hidden parts such as logical operators and include or exclude conditions, with stated limits for X and web; see our[keyword limits by tool](https://syncly.app/blog/social-listening-keyword-limits-what-12-tools-count-(2026)) post.


Before you port a query, check which sources your[social listening platform](https://syncly.app/social/solution/social-listening) collects, then rebuild the exclusion in the new tool's own syntax.


## Key Takeaways


-


A keyword query matches text, not meaning, so fixing an ambiguous brand name takes a sequence of small query changes.


-


Exclusions are typed in the query in Awario and YouScan, and entered in a separate field or condition in Brand24, Sprout and Emplifi.


-


Brand24 applies exclusions to newly collected mentions and Emplifi applies edits to future ones by default, while Sprout says existing topic data is reprocessed.


-


In our invented example, a blunt exclusion lost a relevant post and a context term lost another, so log what each change removes.


Change one thing at a time and keep a sample log, because each exclusion trades junk for risk to relevant posts. The goal is not an empty junk pile but a query whose results you can explain.
